biography.plain_text: Steven M. Mariano is an American entrepreneur who founded and led Patriot National, a Fort Lauderdale insurance-services business focused on workers’ compensation. He previously founded and sold professional staffing company Strategic Outsourcing to Union Planters Bank. His South Florida community work included chairing the Boys & Girls Club of Broward County.

long_biography.plain_text:
Insurance entrepreneur Steven Mariano acquired Guarantee Insurance in 2003 and added fee-based claims and care-management operations alongside it. He later consolidated service companies into Patriot National. He eventually resigned from Patriot’s leadership; Guarantee entered liquidation, and Patriot emerged from bankruptcy under new ownership in 2018.

His support for the University of Miami grew through his cousin Christopher Pizzo, a law graduate who worked at Patriot and arranged a meeting with the law school’s dean. Mariano pledged $1.5 million to launch a programme combining degrees in law, taxation and business administration. Although not a Miami graduate himself, he saw the combined qualifications as a way to prepare students for employers’ demands.

uncertainties: Research date 2026-09-30. Known historical controlling insurance interests support the origin sector and entrepreneurial mechanism independently. Present primary assets are unverified after the documented ownership transition; the primary-industry fallback and Unknown relationship are explicit, separate decisions.

The staffing sale supports entrepreneurship but its consideration, retained stake and relative personal proceeds were not established. Finance & Investments reflects the strongest documented material insurance wealth rather than merely the earliest job. Diversified would overstate the evidence for multiple material personal wealth origins.

Forbes was checked first. Searches covered public personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, Youtube, Vimeo, Flickr, TikTok, Wikipedia and personal/company websites. LinkedIn results were unrelated professionals; the X namesake states a conflicting birth year. Institutional event photographs are not personal accounts. No verified personal or functioning appropriate company destination was found; Trip Advisor and Zillow presented no person-relevant lead.

The immutable May 1964 birth information is compatible with the SEC age but was not independently verified to day and month. No birthplace, secondary nationality or additional residence is proposed. Private contact, people-search and residential data are excluded.

Historical foundation and corporate-directory officer listings do not establish a current principal investment business. The recent lawyer interview is evidence that present interests were not disclosed there, not proof of retirement or absence of assets.

Insurance is the minimum active literal tag. No active staffing or outsourcing concept found; philanthropy facts remain narrative rather than a new taxonomy proposal. Generic investment tags would imply an unverified current portfolio mandate.

The company collapse is central to avoiding a misleading current executive biography. Civil allegations, regulatory findings against a company and the later jury verdict in his claim against lawyers remain distinct. Biographies use only verified corporate outcomes, not disputed accusations.
